target: Jag tvättar mig och klär på mig.
english: I wash up and get dressed.
tip: Two reflexives in one sentence – each needs its own "mig."

target: Hon undervisar barn i engelska på en skola i Malmö.
english: She teaches children English at a school in Malmö.
tip: Swedish prepositions: 'i' (in), 'på' (on/at), 'till' (to), 'från' (from). Choice depends on context.

target: Inte bara blev konserten inställd, utan återbetalningen var också väldigt långsam.
english: Not only was the concert cancelled, but the refund process was also very slow.
tip: "Inte nog med att" = not only ... (emphatic pattern).

target: Hypotesen kunde inte falsifieras i köket.
english: The hypothesis could not be falsified in the kitchen.
tip: "Falsifiera" = falsify. "Kunde inte falsifieras" = could not be falsified.

target: Jag kan inte simma.
english: I can't swim.
tip: "Kan inte" = can't. Negation always after the modal verb in main clauses.

target: Jag har knappast sovit.
english: I have hardly slept.
tip: "Knappast" = hardly / barely – a softer negation.

target: Hon gillar inte vinter.
english: She doesn't like winter.
tip: Swedish double-marks definiteness when using adjectives: 'den stora boken' needs both 'den' and the '-en' suffix.

target: De bor nära centrum.
english: They live near the center.
tip: "Nära" = near. Can be preposition or adverb.

target: Jag tycker inte om det.
english: I don't like it.
tip: "Tycker inte om" = don't like. "Inte" splits "tycker" and "om" (particle).

target: Det spelar inte så stor roll.
english: It doesn't really matter.
tip: Plural definite forms depend on the declension group: '-na' for most en-words, '-en' or '-a' for ett-words in plural.

target: Hur vill du betala just nu snart?
english: How do you want to pay right now soon?
tip: Swedish dropped formal `you` in the 1960s-70s (`du-reformen`). Unlike French/German/Russian, there is no formal pronoun – `du` works for everyone.

target: Tack så mycket för din hjälp med allting idag verkligen.
english: Thank you so much for your help with everything today.
tip: 'Verkligen' (really/truly) – adds emphasis: 'Det var verkligen bra' (It was really good).

target: Det är alltid roligt att lära känna nya människor här.
english: It is always fun to get to know new people here.
tip: 'Alltid' (always) – goes after the verb in main clauses: 'Jag äter alltid frukost'.

target: Sväng till vänster vid nästa korsning.
english: Turn left at the next intersection.
tip: "Vid" means 'at/by.' Directions: till vänster (left), till höger (right), rakt fram (straight).

target: Hon orkade inte mer efter en så lång dag.
english: She couldn't manage anymore after such a long day.
tip: "Orka" = to have the energy/strength for something. Very Swedish.

target: Dricksen ingår alltid i priset på den här restaurangen.
english: The tip is always included in the price at this restaurant.
tip: Tipping is not expected in Sweden – service charge is usually included.

target: Jag väntar utanför dörren.
english: I wait outside the door.
tip: "Utanför" = outside of.

target: Det här är min vän Lisa.
english: This is my friend Lisa.
tip: Swedish adjective comparison: -are (comparative), -ast (superlative). Irregular: bra/bättre/bäst, stor/större/störst.

target: Jag har arbetat här i snart femton år nu.
english: I have worked here for almost fifteen years now.
tip: Group 1 supine: -at ending: 'har arbetat' (has worked), 'har pratat' (has talked).

target: Jag vill gärna veta mer om ditt nya projekt.
english: I would really like to know more about your new project.
tip: Swedish subordinate clauses: 'inte' and other adverbs go before the verb, not after like in main clauses.

target: Jag har alltid älskat svensk natur nu.
english: I have always loved Swedish nature.
tip: "Älska" → "älskat" (Group 1 supine: -at). Time adverbs go between har and supine.

target: Jag behöver en starkare lampa för att kunna läsa bättre.
english: I need a stronger lamp to be able to read better.
tip: "Stark" = strong. Regular comparison: starkare, starkast.

target: Ännu idag minns jag den kvällen verkligen.
english: Even today I remember that evening so vividly.
tip: Remember: 'inte' after the verb in main clauses ('Han köper inte'), but before in subclauses ('att han inte köper').

target: Beställ vad du vill nästa vecka nu!
english: Order whatever you want next week now!
tip: The BIFF rule (Bisats Inte Före Finita verbet) helps remember: in subclauses, 'inte' comes before the finite verb.

target: Redan klockan sex vaknade jag ibland också.
english: Sometimes I even woke up as early as six o'clock.
tip: "Redan" = already. When fronted, V2 rule applies.

target: Ät frukost.
english: Eat breakfast.
tip: Possessives replace the definite suffix: 'min bok' (my book) not 'min boken' – you don't double-mark possession and definiteness.

target: Toast Skagen är en klassiker.
english: Toast Skagen is a classic.
tip: Toast Skagen is a Swedish appetizer with shrimp, mayo, and dill on toast.

target: Vi har dragit i nödtråden.
english: We have pulled the emergency cord.
tip: Sentence adverbs never appear between the subject and verb in Swedish main clauses – they always follow the conjugated verb.

target: Det framkom att ingen visste.
english: It turned out that nobody knew.
tip: Place 'inte' (not) directly after the verb in main clauses: 'Jag äter inte' – but in subclauses it moves before the verb.

target: Hon är lång och syns alltid i en folksamling.
english: She is tall and always stands out in a crowd.
tip: "Lång" = tall/long. Comparative: längre. Superlative: längst.

target: Trevligt att träffas, jag har hört mycket om dig.
english: Nice to meet you, I have heard a lot about you.
tip: Group 2/3 supine: -t ending: 'har köpt' (has bought), 'har bott' (has lived).

target: Meteorologen förutsåg kraftigt snöfall i norr.
english: The meteorologist predicted heavy snowfall in the north.
tip: Swedish adverb placement is tied to clause type – after the verb in main clauses, before it in subclauses starting with att/som/när.

target: Bilen är stor.
english: The car is big.
tip: The adverb position flips between main and subordinate clauses: 'Jag dricker aldrig...' vs. 'att jag aldrig dricker...'

target: Idag är det måndag.
english: Today is Monday.
tip: Days of the week are not capitalized in Swedish.

target: Han har jobbat hela dagen.
english: He has worked all day.
tip: Group 1 supine: -at. Jobba → jobbat.

target: Jag har sprungit fem kilometer.
english: I have run five kilometers.
tip: Abstract and uncountable nouns also take definite suffixes in Swedish: 'maten' (the food), 'vädret' (the weather).

target: Det finns hundra platser ibland här.
english: There are a hundred seats sometimes here.
tip: "Det finns" (there is/are) works for both singular and plural in Swedish.

target: Vi stannade hemma för att det snöade.
english: We stayed home because it was snowing.
tip: "För att" = because (reason). Not to be confused with "för att" = in order to (purpose).

target: Jag vet inte om han kommer till slut.
english: I don't know if he's coming in the end.
tip: "Om" = if/whether in subordinate clauses. Different from "om" = about.

target: Innan vi åker måste vi handla med familjen.
english: Before we leave we need to go shopping with the family.
tip: "Innan" = before (time). Subordinate clause follows.

target: Förlåt att jag är sen, trafiken var helt fruktansvärd.
english: Sorry I am late, the traffic was absolutely terrible.
tip: 'Att' (that/to) introduces subordinate clauses: 'Jag vet att du kan' (I know that you can).

target: Vi har inte setts på väldigt länge nu tyvärr.
english: We have not seen each other for a very long time unfortunately.
tip: 'Tyvärr' (unfortunately) – a common Swedish filler that softens bad news.

target: Min bror bor också i den här staden sedan förra året.
english: My brother has also lived in this city since last year.
tip: 'Sedan' (then/since) – dual meaning: 'sedan igår' (since yesterday), 'sedan gick vi' (then we left).

target: Huset är stort som vi såg i den gamla butiken igår.
english: The house is as big as the one we saw in the old shop yesterday.
tip: Simple definite: "Huset" = the house. Suffix -et for ett-words.

target: Vi kör motorvägen norrut.
english: We drive on the motorway northbound.
tip: E4 is Sweden's main highway running from Helsingborg to Haparanda.

target: Arlanda Express tar tjugo minuter.
english: The Arlanda Express takes twenty minutes.
tip: "Arlanda" is Stockholm's main airport. "Express" trains connect airports to city centers in Sweden.

target: Hon har bott här sedan 2020.
english: She has lived here since 2020.
tip: "Sedan" = since. Used with a point in time.

target: Jag har bott i Stockholm i fem år.
english: I have lived in Stockholm for five years.
tip: Perfekt: har + supine. Group 3 verbs: bo → bott. Used for past with current relevance.

target: Medan vi åt berättade hon historien med familjen.
english: While we ate she told the family a story.
tip: "Medan" = while. Used for simultaneous actions.

target: Dessutom regnar det.
english: Moreover, it's raining.
tip: "Dessutom" = moreover. Sentence adverb – triggers V2.

target: Var snäll och hjälp mig.
english: Please be kind and help me.
tip: "Var snäll och" + imperative is a polite way to make a request.

target: Det här problemet måste vi lösa.
english: We must solve this problem.
tip: Time and manner adverbs have more flexibility, but negation ('inte') and frequency adverbs strictly follow verb-position rules.

target: Jag förstår varför du är upprörd.
english: I understand why you're upset.
tip: `Ni` survives only as the plural 'you' (you all). Some older speakers or very formal contexts use `Ni` for one stranger, but it can actually sound stiff or even sarcastic. Default to `du`.

target: Eftersom det var sent gick vi hem.
english: Since it was late we went home.
tip: "Eftersom" = since/because. Formal reason clause.

target: Restaurangen som ligger på hörnet är ny.
english: The restaurant on the corner is new.
tip: "Som ligger" = that is located. Very common pattern.

target: Vi hoppas att vädret blir bra verkligen.
english: We really hope the weather will be nice.
tip: "Hoppas" is a deponent verb (s-form but active meaning). It takes an att-clause.

target: Jag kan inte sova eftersom det är ljust.
english: I can't sleep because it's light.
tip: "Eftersom" = because/since. Triggers subordinate word order.

target: Öppna dörren.
english: Open the door.
tip: Group 1 imperatives keep the -a: öppna! stänga! → stäng! (Group 2, drop -a).

target: Hastigheten är begränsad till åttio.
english: The speed is limited to eighty kilometers per hour.
tip: "Begränsad till" = limited to. Swedish speed limits: 30-50 urban, 70-120 highways.

target: Hon studerar för att bli läkare.
english: She studies to become a doctor.
tip: "För att" = in order to. Used to express purpose.
